doc.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: From Birdland to Broadway and writing fiction
summary: His second book collects his own stories; he rejects a sequel and experiments with short stories.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, when I was putting together this volume, I decided that the stories of my own experience had a little different color to them. So I saved them all out, just on a hunch. And when this was successful I said to Sheldon, “You know I’ve got another book” I said, “this one’s more of an autobiography, but it’s stories.” And he said, “okay.” So I wrote From Birdland to Broadway, that was my second one. I don’t really want to do Son Of Jazz Anecdotes. I told the best ones in that book and there’s still a lot of stories around, and a lot of the ones that I do from my column are not particularly from the jazz world, they are musician stories from other venues. And if I get some kind of a focus for that I might try making another book out of that. But I am fooling around with some of the stories I couldn’t tell for personal reasons, people who are still alive — but the stories © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-

are so good that I’m using them as plots for short stories and I’m trying to teach myself to write fiction. It’s hard. It’s, I don’t know if I’ll ever get good enough at it to bring it out in public, but it’s something that I play with at home.
